newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $10 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $10 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $10 lower Tuesday in line with losses overnight in London, traders said.
LIFFE cocoa futures slumped Tuesday as Sterling's firmness against the mark weighed on the market. At the midday break, September was down 11 stg at 1,027 stg a tonne, traded 1,041 to 1,024 stg.
Sterling also rose against the dollar overnight, reaching near seven-month highs after an unexpectedly strong rise in British inflation suggested there may be an increase in interest rates this week.

Monday, New York cocoa futures erased early gains and ended slightly lower, pressured by speculative liquidation. September settled off $4 at $1,558 a tonne after ranging from $1,590 to $1,554. Spot July fell the same to $1,536, while the remaining months eased $1 to $4.
Technically, traders said last Thursday's low of $1,525 in September would provide support, followed by $1,514. Resistance was seen near Monday's high of $1,590.

The CFTC Commitments of Traders report released after Monday's close showed speculators (non-commercials and nonreportables) were net long 33,724 lots as of July 1, but did not reflect the recent sharp sell-off.
Non-commercial long positions rose by 6,856 lots in the two weeks ended July 1 to 28,994 lots. Non-commercial short positions rose by 801 lots, to 3,943 lots.
Commercial long positions in the two weeks rose by 644 lots to 57,276 lots, while commercial short positions rose 8,907 lots to 91,000 lots.
Non-reportable long positions rose 2,971 lots to 19,671 lots and nonreportable short positions rose by 763 lots to 10,998 lots.
